qmd-fast is built around one idea: writing technical content should feel as
immediate as editing code. You save the file, and only the block you changed
re-renders — your scroll position, your live canvas, and your warm kernel all stay
exactly as they were. No cold start, no full-page flash, no waiting.

```sh
qmd-fast preview post.qmd   # live at http://127.0.0.1:4321 — edit, and watch one block update
```

{{< video assets/live-edit-light.mp4 dark=assets/live-edit-dark.mp4 caption="Save the file, and only the block you touched re-renders — in place, with scroll and live state preserved." >}}

## One source, many outputs

Write once in plain text and choose the output in the front matter. Every format
shares the same block model, the offline math and highlighting, and the live edit
loop — so anything you learn for one carries to the rest.

::: {.feature-grid}
::: {.feature}
### Blog posts & papers
Prose, math, figures, citations, and cross-references, with executable Python/R
cells and live interactive graphics.

[See an example →](formats.qmd#blog-posts)
:::

::: {.feature}
### Slide decks
A native slide engine: fragments, presenter view, PDF export, code stepping — and
code that actually runs on the slide.

[Open the live deck →](formats.qmd#slide-decks)
:::

::: {.feature}
### Multi-chapter books
A sidebar, numbered chapters, cross-chapter references, and full-text search. These
very docs are a qmd-fast book.

[Read the docs book →](docs/guide/)
:::

::: {.feature}
### Multi-page websites
Navbar, footer, listings, RSS, OpenGraph, and Cmd-K search. This whole site is a
qmd-fast website.

[How this site is built →](formats.qmd#websites)
:::
:::

## Edit the code. The output re-runs in place.

A `{python}` or `{r}` cell runs against a warm kernel. Change a parameter and only
that cell — and the figure it produced — re-renders. The rest of the page never
moves, and the kernel never cold-starts.

{{< video assets/live-code-light.mp4 dark=assets/live-code-dark.mp4 caption="One value changes in the source; the matplotlib figure updates in place, scroll preserved." >}}

## Built the way you would build yours

There is nothing here a screenshot could fake: **this landing page, its
[documentation book](docs/guide/), and the slide deck above are all built and served by
qmd-fast** — from plain `.qmd` files in one repository. If it reads well here, the
framework is doing its job.

::: {.hero}
